passage:
I'm Irawati. Last year Papa kept saying, "No tension, beta, all is well." But he stopped taking the scooter and walked to work, and twice I saw the shop's shutter down early. My brother Asif told me not to ask.
I felt so protected that I felt shut out. Guessing was worse than knowing.
One night I said, "Papa, I'm sixteen. I can handle hearing it. I'm not asking you to fix anything." He was quiet for a while, and then he admitted the shop had been slow for months.
I stopped mentioning the class trip and told him I'd manage with my old phone. I didn't blame him. I just said I'd rather know than guess, and he nodded.

qa.q: What did Irawati notice about how Papa got to work?
qa.a: He stopped taking the scooter and walked to work.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel about being protected from the truth?
qa.a: Irawati felt shut out and anxious, because guessing at what was wrong was harder than knowing.

qa.q: How did Irawati adjust what they asked for without blaming Papa?
qa.a: Irawati stopped mentioning the class trip and said the old phone would do, telling Papa it was better to know than guess.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt when Irawati said they could handle hearing it?
qa.a: After a quiet pause he admitted the shop had been slow, so he may have felt relieved to stop pretending, though probably still worried.

grounding: A parent hides a money problem to protect the teen, who senses it, kindly asks for honesty and adjusts their requests without blame.
